sumInsured: As per Policy Schedule (not provided in extract)

great.name: Restore Benefit: Unlimited Automatic Recharge (reinstatement) after exhaustion
great.quote: The Company agrees to automatically make the re-instatement of up to the base Sum Insured unlimited times in a policy year
great.explanation: Strong restore feature: once your base SI (and certain buffers) are exhausted, the insurer replenishes SI unlimited times within the same policy year (subject to conditions).

great.name: Restore can be used for same illness (with limited exception)
great.quote: Recharge amount can be utilized for same illness except for claim under Any one Illness condition.
great.explanation: Better than standard restores that allow only unrelated illnesses. Here it can be used for the same illness too, except where the policy treats it as 'Any One Illness' (relapse rule).

great.name: Built-in additional Sum Insured buffers: Cumulative Bonus + Inflation Shield (over and above base SI growth)
great.quote: For any single Claim during a Policy Year, the maximum Claim amount payable shall be sum total of Sum Insured, Cumulative Bonus, Inflation Shield.
great.reference: Clause 3, General Conditions Applicable To All The Benefits, point 2(II)
great.explanation: The policy has built-in additional SI buffers (bonus and inflation-linked increase) that increase available coverage beyond base SI (subject to policy rules).

great.name: No Claim Bonus Protect: 50% per year (up to 200%) with partial-claim protection
great.quote: enhance the Sum Insured by 50% flat, on a cumulative basis... provided that no Claim has been paid... or total claim amount payable does not exceed the 25% of the base Sum Insured
great.reference: Clause 3.1.11 Benefit : No Claim Bonus Protect
great.explanation: High renewal bonus rate (50% p.a.) and it can still accrue/continue when total claims are within 25% of base SI—stronger than standard NCB structures.

good.name: PED waiting period: 36 months
good.quote: excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer.
good.explanation: 36 months PED wait is within acceptable market range (GOOD as per your rule set).

good.name: Specific illness waiting period: 24 months
good.quote: shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage
good.explanation: 24 months is standard for specified illnesses/procedures.

good.name: Initial waiting period: 30 days
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident

good.name: Pre-hospitalization cover: 60 days
good.quote: Under Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses, for a period of 60 days immediately prior
good.explanation: Covers eligible pre-hospitalization expenses for 60 days (standard-good).

good.name: Post-hospitalization cover: 90 days
good.quote: Under Post-hospitalization Medical Expenses, for a period of 90 days immediately after
good.explanation: Covers eligible post-hospitalization expenses for 90 days (standard-good).

bad.name: Room rent limit can be capped (proportionate deduction applies if you choose higher room)
bad.quote: If the Policy Schedule states ‘up to 1% of the Sum Insured per day’ as eligible Room Rent, it means the maximum eligible Room Rent... is limited to 1% of the Sum Insured per day of Hospitalization.
bad.explanation: A percentage-based room rent cap can cause significant out-of-pocket and proportionate (ratable) deductions if you stay in a higher category room.

bad.name: Proportionate (ratable) deduction on associated medical expenses if room category exceeds eligibility
bad.quote: The Policyholder/Insured Person shall bear the ratable proportion of the total Associate Medical Expenses... in the proportion of the difference between the Room Rent actually incurred and the Room Rent specified in the Policy Schedule
bad.explanation: If your room is above eligibility (when room rent/category is limited in your schedule), the insurer reduces payout on many linked expenses (surgeon, OT, etc.), increasing your out-of-pocket.

bad.name: Consumables not covered (non-medical items list includes common consumables like gloves, masks etc.)
bad.quote: Any item or condition or treatment specified in List of Non-Medical Items (Annexure – I to Policy Terms & Conditions).
bad.explanation: Consumables such as gloves, masks, kits, etc. are generally excluded via the non-medical items list, leading to out-of-pocket expenses during hospitalization.

bad.name: Domiciliary hospitalization: major common chronic conditions excluded
bad.quote: Any Medical Expenses incurred for the treatment in relation to any of the following diseases shall not be payable under this Benefit : ... Diabetes Mellitus... Hypertension... Arthritis...
bad.explanation: Even though domiciliary cover exists, many common conditions are excluded for home treatment, reducing usefulness of this benefit.

bad.name: Disease / procedure sub-limits may apply (as per policy terms)
bad.quote: For diseases or conditions or procedure that have a specified sub-limit then all related expenses shall be covered up to the sub-limit specified for that disease or condition or procedure.
bad.explanation: The policy allows applying sub-limits for certain diseases/procedures (limits not shown in this extract). Any such sub-limit can materially reduce claim payouts.

unclear.explanation: The default room eligibility for your policy is not visible here; it can materially impact claim payouts. Check your Policy Schedule for exact room category/rent eligibility.

unclear.quote: In the event of total claim amount payable exceeds 25% of the base Sum Insured during any Policy Year, the accrued Cumulative Bonus will be reduced at same rate at which it is accrued
unclear.explanation: NCB is not a simple 'claim resets to zero' structure; reduction depends on whether claims exceed 25% of base SI and by how much. Exact practical impact needs your scenario and schedule details.
